thread:
sara_eng: paging: multiple alerts for dedicated-pool-eta-3 showing p99 request latency > 3s and streaming stalls. customers reporting degraded chat responses. I see queue depth on pool 3 jumping from ~5 to 240.

incident-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-eta-3: p99 latency 3.6s (SLO breach), queue depth 240, warmup pending 18 nodes. Paging matt_oncall.

matt_oncall: on it — taking oncall. initial hypothesis: autoscaler didn't spin up warm instances fast enough; warmup handshake timeouts seen in logs. handoff to leah if escalation needed.

leah_sre: digging into autoscaler logs now. can folks paste recent deploys? any config changes to warmup timeout or node image?

sam_platform: no deploys in the last hour. we pushed a config tweak to batching windows ~4h ago but that was on hosted path, not dedicated. autoscaler config unchanged.

matt_oncall: copying in quick queries:

```# recent metrics
GET /metrics/queues?pool=eta-3&window=15m
queue_depth: max=246 avg=78
warmup_in_flight: 18
ready_nodes: 6 -> decreasing
autoscale_events: 3 failed_handshakes
```

leah_sre: those failed_handshakes look like TLS handshake timeouts during bootstrapping of warm instances. I see increased success latency on init script around 12-18s. warmup timeout is 10s in current runbook.

jane_support: customer-impact note: two large customers on Dedicated reported truncated stream and reconnects. CS has notified them we're investigating and provided mitigation suggestions (retry + backoff).

sara_eng: impact estimate from telemetry: ~4% of requests in last 10m hit p95>1.5s, p99>3s, streaming stalls count increased x8. Token-level cost may spike if retries occur.

matt_oncall: temporary mitigation idea: disable aggressive prefix caching to free up memory on hot nodes and drop batch size floor so more requests get scheduled across nodes. also enable fallback routing to secondary pool (eta-2) for non-sensitive customers.

sam_platform: we can flip fallback routing flag, but need approval for risk. fallback pool has ~20% spare capacity currently. we can add route for requests with header `X-fallback-ok: true`.

leah_sre: action list: 1) flip fallback routing for non-sensitive tenants 2) increase warmup timeout to 45s to allow bootstraps to finish 3) temporarily disable prefix cache on saturated nodes 4) escalate to infra if node images failing init. I'll run 1 and 2.

matt_oncall: +1. please coordinate on sequence. flipping warmup timeout first might allow existing in-flight warmups to succeed; fallback routing will drain queue.

sara_eng: FYI, disabling prefix cache will increase per-token compute slightly but should reduce queue lifetime. good trade for now.

leah_sre: running command to increase warmup timeout:

```# patch autoscaler config
kubectl -n infra patch configmap autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"warmup_timeout_secs":"45"}}'
```

incident-bot: configmap patch accepted. autoscaler warmup_timeout_secs -> 45s.

sam_platform: enabling fallback routing for tenants with header now: toggling feature flag `dedicated.fallback.routing` to true for tier=standard.

incident-bot: feature flag enabled for tier=standard. routing rules updated.

matt_oncall: monitoring queue depth and p99.

[~6 minutes pass]

leah_sre: warmup handshake failures dropped by ~70%. ready_nodes climbing: 6 -> 14. queue_depth trending down 240 -> 52. p99 decreased from 3.6s -> 1.8s. streaming stalls decreasing but still above baseline.

sara_eng: customer impact: CS reports fewer interruptions; one enterprise still seeing intermittent stalls (they are on non-fallback path).

matt_oncall: can we route that customer to fallback temporarily? Need authorization from jane_support or account owner.

jane_support: I've DM'd account owner; they've approved a temporary fallback for 10 mins. apply and monitor.

sam_platform: routing rule patched for that account id -> now on fallback pool. confirm.

incident-bot: routing updated for account 91234 -> fallback pool eta-2.

leah_sre: after routing change, their p99 dropped under 1.2s and stream reconnects stopped. overall p99 now ~1.1s, p95 ~0.4s. queue_depth steady ~18.

matt_oncall: moving to mitigation complete, but need post-incident actions: why did warmup handshakes spike? root cause candidate: init script pulled container images from regional registry that had a hiccup, causing extra latency on boot. second candidate: autoscaler backoff logic treated transient failures as terminal and didn't retry aggressively.

sam_platform: I found errors in init logs: `Tarball extraction timeout` on some nodes and `connection reset by peer` to registry during image pull around identical timestamps. That matches registry transient issue.

leah_sre: follow-ups I want: A) increase warmup timeout to 60s for pools with heavy model loads, B) add exponential retry for handshake failures in autoscaler, C) add pre-warm validation step after node ready to ensure streaming stack is healthy before marking warm. D) improve metrics to surface handshake time distribution.

sara_eng: plus add playbook note to use fallback routing earlier when queue_depth > 100 and warmup_in_flight > 10.

matt_oncall: agree. I'll file an incident postmortem, assign owners. quick owners: registry infra -> sam_platform (investigate registry availability and add retries), autoscaler -> leah_sre (retry/backoff logic), runbook/console -> sara_eng (playbook and thresholds).

jane_support: customer follow-up: I'll send templated status + apology and note we've applied fallback and follow-ups planned.

incident-bot: Incident severity: P2 (SLOs breached, partial customer impact). Start time: 2026-03-14T16:34:04Z (thread_ts 2213334444). Mitigated: 2026-03-14T16:42:00Z (last_message_ts 2213334520).

matt_oncall: closing the paging loop. if anyone sees a regression re-open. great job team :thumbsup:

leah_sre: adding KPT items to backlog now.

sara_eng: will write short postmortem draft and circulate.

[thread ends]
